transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Ethan Liu (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (Nettleworks Head of Platform), Priya Desai (VP Eng), Nathan Cole (Infra), Sofia Ruiz (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Nettleworks evaluating EU on-prem to meet data residency and latency goals. Interested in reserved capacity uplift for Q2, want clear runbook for pilot and KMS/HSM integration details. Agreed to contract amendment draft and pilot scheduling.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick check — can folks see my screen? I have the renewal slides + proposed capacity uplift.
[00:08] Priya (Nettleworks): Yep seeing it, looks good.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda — contract amendment, reserved capacity numbers, EU on-prem pilot scope, then security and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:21] Liam (Nettleworks): Sounds good. We wanna make sure the on-prem plan doesn't blow up our networking timeline. We've got a compliance gate in mid-March.
[00:29] Maya (Redwood SE): Noted. We'll outline minimal network requirements and a fallback (VPC peering) if on-prem takes longer.

[02:05] Jordan: First, renewal. Current contract ends May 31. You're asking for a 30% uplift in reserved tokens/capacity, plus an EU on-prem pilot. Correct?
[02:15] Liam: Yep. Usage in Q4 surprised us — the churn in conversation agents increased token counts. We want predictable unit cost for Q2/Q3.
[02:25] Ethan (CSM): To confirm: current reserved capacity covers ~80 rps sustained at 256 prompt length equivalence, and you requested 110 rps with headroom for 160 rps bursts.
[02:37] Nathan: That's right. Peak is very spiky during hourly batch jobs — we need burst to be smooth; otherwise queues back up.

[04:12] Maya: On the performance side, we recommended keeping a small prefix cache and using quantized model variant for lower-cost inference in non-critical paths. That gives about 18% token cost reduction in our bench.
[04:26] Priya: How does that affect latency? Our customer SLAs are 150ms p95 for short prompts.
[04:33] Maya: The quantized variant we propose adds ~10-20ms p95 in our tests. For your 150ms SLO, we typically recommend mixed routing: critical routes to full-precision in Dedicated, non-critical to quantized.
[04:45] Priya: Ok — we'll need route-level configs.

[06:00] Liam: On the EU on-prem pilot: what's the minimal footprint? We don't want to provision a big cluster for pilot.
[06:09] Maya: Minimal pilot can run on 2x A100-equivalent nodes for inference with a small staging dataset; that covers 30-40 rps realistic load. For full production you'd want 6-8 nodes depending on model size and burst profile.
[06:22] Nathan: Are those cloud VMs or bare-metal?
[06:26] Maya: Either. We support the on-prem package with containerized runtime and orchestration. For EU on-prem we recommend customer-managed hardware or co-located racks.

[08:10] Sofia (Security): Talk to me about KMS and audit logs. Our policy requires keys in our HSM and 365-day immutable audit retention.
[08:21] Maya: We support external KMS/HSM integrations. For the on-prem control plane we'll provide hooks to your KMS via KMIP / vault plugin. Audit logs can be streamed to your SIEM; retention windows are configurable — we can set an immutable retention lifecycle, but we need to align on storage capacity.
[08:38] Sofia: Also need SOC2 artifacts and penetration test summary.
[08:42] Jordan: We'll share redwood SOC2 Type 2 and our pen test executive summary. I'll strip anything sensitive per your redaction notes.

[10:00] Priya: Back to cost — reserved capacity vs on-demand pricing. If we commit monthly, what's the delta?
[10:09] Jordan: For reserved commitment we can provide ~28-35% discount vs on-demand depending on term and volume. EU on-prem includes a platform fee plus per-node license; the uplift in reserved capacity buys you lower per-token unit economics on hosted/Dedicated than ad-hoc bursts.
[10:25] Ethan: Also note billed tokens in on-prem differ slightly because of retained caches and local network overhead — we'll provide an overlay for estimates.

[12:55] Liam: Timeline — compliance gate mid-March. Can we do pilot in Feb to validate latency before we go into that gate?
[13:03] Maya: Yes, we can target a 2-week pilot starting Feb 16 if hardware/network is ready. We need your network CIDR allowances and KMS provisioning by Feb 12 to hit that.
[13:12] Nathan: Feb 12 is tight but doable if we prioritize it.

[15:40] Sofia: One more security point: does Redwood support customer-managed audit log encryption and HSM key rotation policies?
[15:47] Maya: Yes. Keys stay in your HSM; we call them via KMIP and keys never leave. Rotation is supported; there is a brief cache eviction we coordinate during rotation windows.

[18:02] Jordan: Competitor noise — you mentioned AtlasCloud in your RFP. Any particular features pushing you that direction?
[18:09] Priya: Mostly pricing and on-prem story. Atlas is pushing a turnkey private cluster but their observability is weak. We like Redwood's console and rollout features.
[18:18] Jordan: Good to know. We'll highlight the rollouts/canary paths + cost overlay in the SOW.

[22:00] Maya: Technical note — KV cache warm-up for your conversational flows matters. If you can provide a warm start dataset we can preload prefixes and avoid early tail latencies in pilot.
[22:12] Nathan: We can run a warm start export from prod; I'll coordinate with Maya on format.

[27:30] Ethan: Contract language — you asked about amendments to include EU on-prem terms and reserved capacity addendum. We'll propose a one-page amendment for term extension (12 months) and a schedule for reserved units.
[27:42] Liam: Do we need legal redlines now or after pricing?
[27:46] Jordan: We'll send pricing first, but we can include standard redlines for data residency and liability in the amendment.

[32:00] Priya: Operational runbook — we want a clear rollback/fallback plan: if on-prem node fails, traffic should route to hosted EU region.
[32:09] Maya: Agreed. We'll supply a failover playbook: health checks, automatic fallback policy, and a manual degrade mode with reduced token quality but preserved availability.
[32:20] Priya: That fallback latency to hosted EU — what's realistic?
[32:25] Maya: On failure, failover to hosted EU adds ~30-60ms depending on route and model variant; cold KV cache may add additional 80-120ms for first requests.

[36:55] Nathan: For billing: can we get a blended invoice for on-prem license + reserved hosted capacity? Our finance team prefers single monthly invoice.
[37:03] Jordan: Yes, we can produce a consolidated invoice. We'll note tax/regulatory implications for cross-border billing in the amendment.

[40:21] Sofia: One more — can you provide a list of required firewall ports and egress endpoints?
[40:27] Maya: I'll send a succinct list: control plane gRPC endpoints, metrics ingestion, S3 endpoints (for model artifacts), and KMS endpoints. We'll make it minimal for pilot.

[44:00] Jordan: Quick recap and next steps: Jordan sends pricing + amendment (due 2/6); Maya sends pilot runbook + firewall/KMS checklist and schedules tech deep dive (propose 2/10); Nettleworks confirms throughput numbers and required retention (due 2/9); Sofia sends security doc list (due 2/8). Pilot target window Feb 16–27.
[44:21] Liam: That works. Thanks everyone.
[44:27] Priya: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.

References mentioned: SOW draft link (shared in chat), pilot runbook template (will be shared via email), SOC2 Type 2 PDF (shared link to redacted copy).
